storyQualifications.fact: The 2023 Moon Knight annual selects MacKay's material; the included item is the whole issue.
The Infinite Destinies collection expands to exactly eight annuals. Its Black Cat annual repeats an earlier selected issue.
Blood Hunt selects the five main issues, not the event tie-ins.
The Spider-Verse source calls the selection an anthology contribution; its source year and the provider series start differ and require review.
Only the named MacKay contributions in the selected Spider-Verse issues are in scope; each selected item is the whole issue.
The two named Free Comic Book Day issues are whole issues and may include other writers.

collectionExpansion.sourceReference: Infinite Destinies / Infinite Fury (2021), eight annuals
collectionExpansion.facts: The collection contents name the eight annuals in the source expansion order. Google Books labels Amazing Spider-Man Annual #2 by the parent run's 2018 start; the other index and the provider label the annual 2021. Black Cat Annual is repeated elsewhere in the source. These whole issues contain contributions from other writers, and the two independently selected Black Cat issues are not additions to the eight-annual collection.

evidence.fact: The 2018 announcement expands MDO as Marvel Digital Original and identifies Jed MacKay and Travel Foreman for the Daughters of the Dragon series.

titleAliases.providerEvidence: The same provider series and three issue details give the selected numbers, 2018 series start and Jed Mackay as a writer; issue #2 spells out Marvel Digital Original.

evidence.fact: The review identifies Superior Octopus #1 and an October 3, 2018 release; it lists Christos Gage, not the issue's other contributor, as writer.

titleAliases.providerEvidence: The provider's issue detail also lists Jed Mackay as a writer. The extra digit in the provider series name is not a second issue.

missingProviderCredits.providerFact: The issue detail has no writer credits.

evidence.fact: The review identifies Jed MacKay as writer and gives the November 13, 2019 release date.

missingProviderCredits.disposition: Retain the exact selected issue. Do not invent a provider credit.

missingProviderCredits.providerFact: The issue detail lists three writers but omits Jed MacKay.

evidence.fact: This anthology index lists Jed MacKay and the other writers separately for issue #4.
The independent index lists Jed MacKay with the other three writers and gives the February 23, 2011 release date.

missingProviderCredits.disposition: Retain the exact selected issue. Do not alter the provider's credits.

evidence.fact: The 2014-2015 anthology's second issue went on sale January 14, 2015 and credits Jed MacKay.
A different issue #2 went on sale June 10, 2015 and credits Mike Costa.

sourceDecision.decidedBy: Copilot coordinator acting as source reviewer
sourceDecision.reason: The selected issue is the anthology contribution credited to MacKay; the 2015-series issue credits Mike Costa. The source's year normally names the series start, so its 2015 label conflicts with the selected 2014 series.
sourceDecision.inputDigestBasis: The factual ledger digest computed with this reviewedInputLedgerDigest field null.

evidence.fact: A review calls the issue #78.BEY and credits Jed MacKay.
A review published November 17, 2021 calls the same Daughters of the Dragon story #78.1 and credits Jed MacKay.

bridges.decisionNeeded: Review the source-to-provider number alias; the checklist can retain the source's #78.BEY spelling.

evidence.fact: A preview names #92.BEY, its March 16, 2022 release and writers Jed MacKay, Cody Ziglar and Zeb Wells.
An independent index lists the same release date and writers for #92.BEY.

bridges.decisionNeeded: Review the source-to-provider number alias against the provider receipt; the checklist can retain the source's #92.BEY spelling.

ownerDecision: One list in release order, so his series interleave as he wrote them (Recommended)
